title: Gold Steadies Near $3,565 as Fed Rate Path and AI Stocks
summary: Gold holds near $3,565 as traders weigh Federal Reserve rate hikes against AI stock rebounds. Third monthly loss exceeds 6% amid sticky inflation concerns.
body_markdown:
**Officially launched on November 26, 2026.**


#### 💡 TL;DR


- Gold steadied near $3,565 per ounce on November 26, 2026, after sinking to a 15-month low earlier in the week.
- Federal Reserve inflation data reinforced expectations of December rate hikes, pressuring non-interest-bearing gold prices downward.
- AI technology stocks rebounded Thursday, lifting global equities and creating competing market forces against traditional safe-haven assets.


Gold prices steadied near $3,565 per ounce on November 26, 2026, as traders navigated conflicting market signals from Federal Reserve monetary policy and a sharp rebound in artificial intelligence technology equities. The precious metal posted a modest weekly gain after earlier plunging to a 15-month low, underscoring the volatility gripping commodity markets as investors reassess inflation risks and central bank responses.


## Fed Rate Expectations Pressure Gold


The Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge for October, released November 25, 2026, reinforced market expectations that the central bank will implement interest rate hikes when policymakers convene in December. Spot gold traded at $3,567.67 per ounce at 7:45 a.m. Singapore time, holding below the psychologically significant $4,000 threshold since November 11. Higher borrowing costs typically diminish gold's appeal because the metal generates no yield, making interest-bearing assets more attractive by comparison.


The yellow metal is on track for its third consecutive monthly decline exceeding 6%, extending a retreat from January's record high that accelerated after the US-Iran conflict drove energy costs sharply higher. Traders are now pricing in the likelihood of additional rate increases in early 2027 if price pressures persist, creating sustained headwinds for non-yielding commodities.


## AI Stocks Rally Lifts Global Markets


Global equity markets climbed Thursday as investors in Europe and Asia followed a recovery in AI-related stocks, which had suffered steep losses in recent sessions. US cash markets remained closed for the Thanksgiving holiday, limiting trading volume but not dampening the broader risk-on sentiment. The rebound in[AI technology stocks](https://emergent.sh/news/ai-stocks-surge-market-hits-new-highs) provided a competing narrative to gold's traditional safe-haven role, pulling capital toward growth assets as optimism returned to the semiconductor and cloud computing sectors.


The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index extended its winning streak to five consecutive weeks, further weighing on dollar-denominated gold prices. A stronger US currency makes bullion more expensive for holders of other currencies, reducing international demand. Silver slipped 0.1% to $41.50 per ounce, while platinum gained and palladium edged lower in related precious metals trading.


## Choppy Trading Reflects Policy Uncertainty


The week's volatile price action reflects deep uncertainty about the Federal Reserve's policy trajectory and the durability of the AI stock recovery. Gold dropped to its lowest level in 15 months earlier in the week before stabilizing, a pattern that underscores how sensitive commodity markets have become to inflation data releases and central bank communications. Market participants are closely monitoring whether sticky inflation will force the Fed into a more aggressive tightening cycle than previously anticipated.


According to Bloomberg data, bullion has remained range-bound between $3,500 and $3,600 for most of November as traders await clearer signals on both monetary policy and geopolitical risk premiums. The metal's traditional role as an inflation hedge has been complicated by the Fed's hawkish stance, creating a tug-of-war between competing investment narratives.


## What This Means


Gold's ability to hold above $3,500 despite mounting rate hike expectations demonstrates residual safe-haven demand, but the metal faces structural headwinds as long as the Federal Reserve maintains its inflation-fighting posture. The rebound in AI stocks signals that risk appetite remains intact in pockets of the technology sector, potentially limiting capital flows into defensive assets. Investors should watch December's Fed meeting closely, as any deviation from expected tightening could trigger sharp moves in both gold and equity markets heading into 2027.
